title: Hosted Inference: Cost-Fallback & Telemetry Normalization 1.2 Release Notes (Pre-release)
summary:
> **Archived 2026-06-30:** this page is superseded by "Hosted Inference: Cost-Fallback & Telemetry Normalization 1.2 Release Notes" and is kept for reference only.

The 1.2 release adds a Cost-Fallback policy engine to hosted inference and a normalized telemetry stage for cost attribution. The goal is clearer fallback visibility, billing signals that match runtime decisions, and less double-counting when requests fall through several model variants.
highlights: Cost-Fallback engine: a deterministic policy layer that picks fallback variants using a configurable cost threshold plus fidelity constraints.
Telemetry Normalization v1: new pipeline stage that removes duplicate token-attribution events across variant handoffs and retries.
Fallback annotations per request, shown in Console and in API response headers.
Billing hook: optional trial mode that simulates invoicing changes for 14 days with no effect on charges.
SDK updates: client-side flag to opt into fallback transparency headers (Python/Node 1.2.0+).
compatibility_notes: Runtime and billing remain backward compatible. Consumers of legacy billing callbacks should make sure their webhook handlers accept the new 'x-redwood-fallback-reason' header. Upgrading the SDK is recommended for transparent fallback headers; clients that stay on older SDKs keep the previous response shape with less visibility.
impact_table:
| Area | Change | Customer Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Serving runtime | Cost-Fallback engine on by default for low-tier routes | Different model variants may be chosen at peak load | Use rollout controls / opt-out guide |
| Billing & metering | Normalization deduplicates attribution events | Fewer 'per-token' invoiced events visible in reconciliations (expected) | Billing simulator; reconciliations align within the cycle |
| Console | Fallback timeline and per-request annotations | Extra UI column and export fields | Docs + quickstart |
| SDKs | New response headers and opt-in flags | No breakage, richer diagnostics | Upgrade to SDK 1.2.0+ |
rollout_timeline:
1) 2026-06-16: Canary on 5% of hosted traffic in us-west-2.
2) 2026-06-23: Observability review; expand to 25% if no regressions.
3) 2026-06-29: Billing reconciliation test with sandbox customers.
4) Full worldwide enablement and billing switch: dates to be confirmed after reconciliation test.
upgrade_and_migration_steps: Step 1: Check Cost-Fallback policy defaults under Console > Routing > Fallback Policies and flag routes with custom targeting.
Step 2: Enterprise contracts that require a locked variant should open a support ticket to pin the variant or opt out of Cost-Fallback.
Step 3: Update downstream billing webhook consumers to ignore unknown headers; optionally handle 'x-redwood-fallback-reason'.
Step 4: Turn on the Billing Simulator in Console > Billing > Simulators for a 14-day preview of normalized billing (no real charges).
Step 5: Move client SDKs to 1.2.0+ to receive fallback annotations in response headers.
configuration_table:
| Config | Default | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| fallback.cost_threshold_pct | 30 | Percentage over baseline cost allowed before fallback triggers |
| fallback.fidelity_floor | medium | Minimum fidelity for fallback target variants |
| telemetry.dedup_window_ms | 500 | Window for de-duplicating token attribution events |
| billing.simulator.enabled | false | Admin toggle for invoicing preview without charges |
telemetry_and_alerts:
Collected signals and monitoring:
- Events: 'fallback.choice', 'fallback.eviction', 'telemetry.normalization.delta'.
- Dashboards: 'Fallback Rate by Route', 'Normalized vs Raw Token Delta'.
- Alerts: 'Fallback rate > 15% for 5m' (P2), 'Normalization delta > 10% for a billing window' (P3).
If fallback rates climb, check KV-cache hit rates, variant capacity and cost profiles. A normalization alert signals reconciliation variance; reach out to billing-ops before changing routing.
rollback_plan:
1) Set 'fallback.enabled' to false at service level (Console or API) to halt policy-based variant selection.
2) Disable normalization via 'telemetry.normalization.enabled' = false in Admin feature-flags (safe for 1-hour windows).
3) For invoice anomalies, enable billing.simulator, run reconciliation and ask finance-ops to hold invoice dispatch.
4) Gather the last 72h of 'fallback.choice' and 'telemetry.normalization.delta' events and file an incident per the oncall runbook.

known_issues:
- Under multi-region failover combined with a retry storm, deduplication can undercount attribution; SRE may raise dedup_window_ms temporarily.
- SDKs older than 1.1.5 do not expose the new header metadata.
- Customers behind third-party metering proxies that depend on raw token events should validate with the Billing Simulator first.
faq:
Q: Does normalized telemetry change my bill?
A: It removes double-counting across retries and handoffs. Real usage is kept, though line items may shift. Check the Billing Simulator for projections.

Q: Can Cost-Fallback be turned off per route?
A: Yes, via per-route override in Console. Contracts needing strict variant selection should go through the account team.

Q: What happens if early invoices show a >15% delta?
A: Nothing is auto-billed unilaterally; billing ops will contact affected customers and reconcile manually.
